p: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" (תְּהִלִּים כג, ד).
— “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me” (Psalms 23:4).
בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קפט עַמּוּד א)
— In the holy Zohar on this parashah (189a)
דָּרַשׁ פָּסוּק זֶה כְּנֶגֶד יוֹסֵף:
— it expounded this verse corresponding to Joseph:
יוֹסֵף אֲזַל בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת,
— Joseph walked in the valley of the shadow of death,
וְנַחֲתוּ לֵיהּ לְמִצְרַיִם,
— and brought him down to Egypt,
שְׁכִינְתָּא הֲוַת עִמֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵי.
— yet the Shechinah was with him, etc.
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (סוֹטָה לו:):
— And this is what they taught in the Gemara (Sotah 36b):
"לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לט, יא) –
— “to do his work” (Genesis 39:11) –
אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה נִתְכַּוְּונוּ.
— Rabbi Yochanan said: this teaches that both of them intended to commit a transgression.

p: וְרָאִיתִי לְאֶחָד שֶׁהִקְשָׁה:
— And I saw an author who raised a difficulty:
הָא אַשְׁכְּחַן (שַׁבָּת נו.) רַבִּי דְּאָתֵי מִדָּוִד
— behold we find (Shabbat 56a) that Rebbe, who descended from King David,
מְהַפֵּךְ וְדָרֵישׁ בִּזְכוּתֵיהּ דְּדָוִד,
— turns about and expounds in defense of David’s merit;
וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָתֵי מִזַּרְעָא דְּיוֹסֵף כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת כ.),
— whereas Rabbi Yochanan descended from the seed of Joseph as written in Berakhot (20a),
וְלָמָּה דָּרַשׁ לְחוֹבָתוֹ,
— so why did he expound to Joseph's detriment,
כֵּיוָן דִּפְלִיגֵי בָּזֶה בַּגְּמָרָא
— since the Sages disagree on this point in the Gemara,
וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר "מְלַאכְתּוֹ מַמָּשׁ"?
— and he should have adopted the view that it was his literal labor?
גַּם יֵשׁ לְהָבִין כָּל עִיקָּר:
— Furthermore it must be understood fundamentally:
לָמָּה דָּרְשׁוּ "לַעֲשׂוֹת צְרָכָיו נִכְנַס",
— why did the Sages expound “he entered to perform his desires”,
וְלֹא הָפְכוּ בִּזְכוּתוֹ שֶׁל צַדִּיק?
— and not invert the text in favor of the righteous one?
וְיוֹתֵר קָשֶׁה בְּמַה שֶּׁמָּצִינוּ (מְגִילָּה יד:)
— And an even greater difficulty arises in what we find in Megillah (14b)
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ בְּדָוִד שֶׁאָמַר לָהּ לַאֲבִיגַיִל: "הִשָּׁמְעִי לִי",
— where they expounded regarding David that he said to Abigail: “Yield to me”,
אָמְרָה לוֹ: "לֹא תִהְיֶה זֹאת וְגוֹמֵר",
— and she replied: “This shall be no grief unto you, etc.”,
וְהוּא דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין רֶמֶז בַּכָּתוּב,
— which is an idea having no overt textual hint in Scripture,
וְלָמָּה דָּרְשׁוּ כֵּן עַל דָּוִד?
— so why did they expound thus concerning David?
וַהֲלֹא יִקְשֶׁה עֲלֵיהֶם מַה שֶּׁשָּׁאַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
— Would not the sharp challenge that Rabbi Yehudah ben Bateira posed to Rabbi Akiva apply to them:
"בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ אַתָּה עָתִיד לִיתֵּן אֶת הַדִּין:
— “Either way you are destined to give an accounting:
אִם כִּדְבָרֶיךָ – הַתּוֹרָה כִּסַּתּוּ וְאַתָּה מְגַלֶּה אוֹתוֹ,
— if it is as you say, the Torah concealed it and you reveal it,
וְאִם לָאו – אַתָּה מוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק" (שַׁבָּת צו: סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
— and if not, you cast an evil slander upon that righteous man” (Shabbat 96b),
וְכֵן יִקְשֶׁה: לָמָּה תָּלוּ בּוֹ בְּדָוִד חֵטְא כָּזֶה שֶׁלֹּא נִכְתַּב בַּפָּסוּק?
— and likewise here: why attach such a sin to David that is unwritten in the verse?

h: The Protection Given to the Righteous

p: אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת זֶהוּ רַק לְמַעֲלָתוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף וְדָוִד,
— However in truth this was expounded solely for the spiritual greatness of Joseph and David,
שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: "וְלֹא יַעֲזֹב אֶת חֲסִידָיו לְעוֹלָם נִשְׁמָרוּ" (תְּהִלִּים לז, כח).
— which illustrates the verse: “and He does not forsake His pious ones; they are preserved forever” (Psalms 37:28).
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" –
— And this is: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me”—
יוֹסֵף אֲזַל בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת.
— Joseph walked in the shadow of death.
דְּאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה פה, ב):
— For it is stated in Bereishit Rabbah (85:2):
"אַף זוֹ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
— “This woman too intended for the sake of Heaven,
דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
— for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
רוֹאָה הָיְתָה בָּאַסְטְרוֹלוֹגִין שֶׁלָּהּ שֶׁעֲתִידָה לְהַעֲמִיד מִמֶּנּוּ בֵּן,
— she foresaw in her astrological charts that she was destined to establish a son from him,
וְלֹא הָיְתָה יוֹדַעַת אִם מִמֶּנָּה אִם מִבִּתָּהּ וְכוּלֵי".
— yet did not know whether from herself or from her daughter (Asenath), etc.”
וּמִסְּתָמָא כֵּיוָן שֶׁצָּפְתָה הִיא,
— And presumably, since she foresaw this,
בְּוַדַּאי יוֹסֵף הִרְגִּישׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְשָׁרְשָׁהּ,
— Joseph certainly sensed that he had a soul-connection to her root,
וּבְוַדַּאי הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מָצָא לוֹ הֶיתֵּר עַל פִּי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה:
— and the evil inclination undoubtedly formulated a halakhic justification based on Torah principles:
דְּאַף דִּבְעוּלַת בַּעַל יֵשׁ לָהֶם,
— for even though Noahides are forbidden to married women,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם כֵּיוָן שֶׁמְּמָאֶנֶת בּוֹ, הֲרֵי הִיא כִּגְרוּשָׁה שֶׁלָּנוּ,
— nevertheless, since she actively refused Potiphar, she became halakhically like a divorcée,
שֶׁבִּבְנֵי נֹחַ תָּלוּי הַגֵּירוּשִׁין בָּהּ גַּם כֵּן וִיכוֹלָה לִפְרוֹשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ,
— for among Noahides divorce is contingent upon the woman as well and she can withdraw from him,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ״ם (פֶּרֶק ט מֵהִלְכוֹת מְלָכִים הֲלָכָה ח).
— as Maimonides wrote (Hilkhot Melakhim 9:8).

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Yisrael Kedoshim 10:16: “According to the one who says, ‘He entered to attend to his own needs’ (Sotah 36b), it appears that Joseph erred in this. He knew that he had been sold to Egypt and to that very house, and that he certainly had to bring out from there a holy spark and great wealth; and he thought as well, perhaps it is from her, and imagined that his desire was in holiness. Then his father’s image was revealed to him, that is, the attribute of ‘truth to Jacob’ (Micah 7:20), and he saw the truth: that it was the incitement of the evil inclination and not from the side of holiness. For in truth a child born from her would not be his son at all, and a holy spark cannot be brought out in such a way at all. And that this came before him at all, that she should desire him, even though ‘the cursed does not cleave to the blessed,’ since one who has no connection has no desire at all, was through her daughter whom she raised.”

And that this came before him at all, that she should desire him, even though ‘the cursed does not cleave to the blessed,’ since one who has no connection has no desire at all, was through her daughter whom she raised.”

p: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיְהִי כְּהַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לט, יא),
— And this is what Scripture states: “And it came to pass on such a day (ke-hayom hazeh)” (Genesis 39:11),
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם נִדְרַשׁ "הַיּוֹם" עַל יוֹם הַמְּיוּחָד שֶׁהוּא שַׁבָּת
— and throughout rabbinic literature “the day” is expounded as the singular day, which is Shabbat
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּרָא א),
— (as written in Midrash Tanchuma, Vayeira 1),
וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ (בְּשׁוֹחֵר טוֹב תְּהִלִּים צה, ז)
— and so they expounded in Midrash Tehillim (95:7)
פָּסוּק "הַיּוֹם אִם בְּקֹלוֹ תִשְׁמָעוּ" עַל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת.
— the verse “today, if you will hear His voice” as referring to the Sabbath day.
וְהוּא, דְּ"יוֹם" הוּא לְשׁוֹן אוֹר,
— And this is because “day” is an expression of light,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ה),
— as stated: “And God called the light day” (Genesis 1:5),
וְשַׁבָּת יֵשׁ בּוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת מֵאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— and Shabbat contains the manifestation of the Primordial Light,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר (סִימָן קס):
— as written in Sefer HaBahir (section 160):
לָקַח שְׁבִיעִי וְשָׂם לָהֶם בִּמְקוֹמוֹ,
— He took the seventh and set it in their place,
וְלָכֵן נִקְרָא שַׁבָּת בְּיִחוּד בְּשֵׁם "יוֹם" שֶׁהוּא אוֹר,
— therefore Shabbat is uniquely titled “day” signifying light,
וּשְׁאָר הַיָּמִים נִקְרְאוּ גַּם כֵּן "יוֹם" עַל דֶּרֶךְ הַשְׁאָלָה מֵאוֹר הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ.
— whereas the weekdays are called “day” metaphorically based on sunlight.
וּכְתִיב "הַזֶּה" –
— And Scripture writes “this” (hazeh) –
שֶׁקְּדוּשַׁת הַשַּׁבָּת הָיָה מְפוֹרָשׁ לְפָנָיו
— indicating that the holiness of Shabbat stood tangible before him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוֹרֶה לְשׁוֹן "הַזֶּה" כְּמַרְאֶה בְּאֶצְבַּע.
— as demonstrated by the term “this”, like pointing with a finger.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ "יוֹם הַהוּא" עַל עוֹלָם הַבָּא
— And just as “that day” is expounded as the World to Come
שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה אָז אוֹר בְּחִינַת "הוּא",
— wherein the light of the transcendent “He” (concealed realm) will be unveiled,
כֵּן נִדְרַשׁ "הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" עַל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
— so is “this day” expounded upon the Sabbath day
שֶׁמְּפוֹרָשׁ לְנֶגֶד עַיִן קְדוּשַׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, אוֹר כִּי טוֹב.
— wherein the holiness of Shabbat is manifest before our eyes, an illumined light that is good.

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Vayera 1: “You find that not all the eighteen benedictions (of the Amidah) recited each day are in praise of the Holy One, blessed be He. In fact, only the first three and the final three are in praise of Him, while the twelve intervening prayers allude to human needs. It is for this reason that we do not say the eighteen benedictions on the Sabbath. For, if it should happen that a loved one was ill at home at the time of praying, the worshipper would be reminded of it while reciting the prayer ‘Who healeth the ills of His people’ and would become depressed. Inasmuch as the Sabbath was given to Israel for sanctification, for joy and rest and not for sorrow, one must recite the first three blessings and the final three blessings (of the Amidah) and replace the intervening ones with the prayer of Rest. Hence, David proclaimed: Seven times a day do I praise Thee, because of Thy righteous ordinances (Ps. 119:164). The word seven in this verse refers to the seven benedictions recited on the Sabbath. What other day could this verse refer to, if not the day of rest, which is unlike any other? For it is said: Remember the Sabbath day and keep it holy (Exod. 20:8)—in every respect, even from in the pursuit of thy business and speaking thereof (Isa. 58:13).”

paragraphs.text: Sefer HaBahir 160: “Rabbi Berekhya sat and expounded: What do we mean when we speak each day of ‘the World to Come’? We translate it as ‘the world that is coming.’ This teaches that before the world was created, the thought arose to create a great light to illuminate it. Rav Tzadok explains the significance of the seventh day through this teaching.

p: "וַיָּבֹא הַבַּיְתָה לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לט, יא),
— “And he came into the house to do his work” (Genesis 39:11),
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (קצ עַמּוּד ב):
— and it is stated in the holy Zohar (190b):
יוֹמָא דְּיֵצֶר הָרָע שָׁלְטָא בְּעָלְמָא וְכוּלֵי,
— the day when the evil inclination asserts dominion in the world, etc.,
אֵימָתַי?
— when is it?
יוֹמָא דְּאָתֵי בַּר נָשׁ לְאִתְתָּבָא בִּתְיוּבְתָּא עַל חוֹבוֹי אוֹ לְאִשְׁתַּדְּלָא בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְכוּלֵי.
— the day when a man comes to repent over his sins or to immerse in Torah, etc.
וְזֶהוּ בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא זְמַן תְּשׁוּבָה,
— And this corresponds to Shabbat which is the time of repentance,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "טוֹב לְהֹדוֹת לַה'" (תְּהִלִּים צב, ב),
— as stated: “It is good to confess/give thanks unto Hashem” (Psalms 92:2),
וּכְתִיב: "וּמוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָם" (מִשְׁלֵי כח, יג),
— and written: “and whoso confesses and forsakes them shall obtain mercy” (Proverbs 28:13),
וְכֵן שַׁבָּת זְמַן מְיוּחָד לַתּוֹרָה.
— and likewise Shabbat is uniquely dedicated to Torah.
וְזֶהוּ "לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ" –
— And this is “to do his work” –
דְּאִיהוּ מְלַאכְתּוֹ דְּבַר נָשׁ בְּהַאי עָלְמָא,
— which is the authentic work of man in this world (Torah study),
וּכְדֵין יֵצֶר הָרָע נָחִית לְאַסְטָאָה לִבְנֵי נָשָׁא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
— and right then the evil inclination descends to lead mankind astray, as written in the Zohar.
וּבֶטַח מָצָא לוֹ הֶיתֵּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ,
— And the inclination surely fabricated a pseudo-halakhic permission as we noted,
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת" –
— and concerning this it is stated: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death”—
דְּיוֹסֵף אֲזַל בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת.
— for Joseph walked in that shadow of death.
מִכָּל מָקוֹם: "לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי",
— Nevertheless: “I will fear no evil, for You are with me”,
וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "רַגְלֵי חֲסִידָיו יִשְׁמֹר" (שְׁמוּאֵל א ב, ט).
— and Hashem, blessed be He, “will keep the feet of His pious ones” (I Samuel 2:9).

p: וּלְזֶה דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְמַעֲלָתוֹ
— And for this purpose did Rabbi Yochanan expound in Joseph's ultimate praise:
"וַיְהִי וְגוֹמֵר לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלַאכְתּוֹ" –
— “And it came to pass, etc., to do his work”—
שֶׁנִּכְנַס לְאִשְׁתַּדְּלָא בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
— that he entered to immerse himself in Torah,
דְּאִיהוּ מְלַאכְתּוֹ דְּבַר נָשׁ,
— which is the true spiritual vocation of man,
וְאָז בָּא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְפַתּוֹתוֹ.
— and then the evil inclination assaulted him to seduce him.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "מְלַמֵּד שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם וְכוּלֵי",
— And this explains his statement: “teaching that both of them, etc.,”
שֶׁמָּצָא מָקוֹם הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע גַּם בְּיוֹסֵף לְפַתּוֹתוֹ,
— for the inclination found a subtle foothold to entice Joseph,
רַק שֶׁנִּשְׁמַר מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— only that he was divinely safeguarded by Hashem,
וּכְמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְלֹא יַעֲזֹב אֶת חֲסִידָיו לְעוֹלָם נִשְׁמָרוּ".
— as it is stated: “and He does not forsake His pious ones; they are preserved forever”.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי" (תְּהִלִּים כג, ד),
— And upon this Scripture states: “Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me” (Psalms 23:4),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַצִּילוֹ עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁעֶנֶת שֶׁהוּא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
— meaning that sometimes Hashem rescues man via the “staff” of Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ (חֲגִיגָה יד.):
— as expounded in Chagigah (14a):
"מַשְׁעֵן וּמַשְׁעֵנָה כֹּל מִשְׁעַן לֶחֶם וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה ג, א) –
— “the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, etc.” –
הַכֹּל עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
— all expounded as referring to words of Torah.
וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (סוֹטָה לו:):
— And this is like what they taught in the Gemara (Sotah 36b):
שֶׁבָּאתָה דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו וְנִרְאֲתָה לוֹ בַּחַלּוֹן וְכוּלֵי,
— that the visage of his father appeared to him in the window, etc.,
וְהַיְינוּ מִדַּת אֱמֶת,
— which represents the attribute of Truth (Jacob),
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב" (מִיכָה ז, כ),
— as stated: “You will show truth to Jacob” (Micah 7:20),
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה רָאָה וַיָּנָס הַחוּצָה.
— and through this he perceived the reality and fled outside.
וּמֵהַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ גַּם כֵּן מַשְׁמָע שֶׁדָּרַשׁ:
— And from the holy Zohar it likewise appears that it expounded:
"וְאֵין אִישׁ וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לט, יא) –
— “and there was none of the men, etc.” –
שֶׁלֹּא הִתְגַּבֵּר בְּכֹחוֹ עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
— that he did not overpower the evil inclination by his own strength alone,
עַד שֶׁמָּצְאָה מְעַט שְׁלִיטָה בּוֹ,
— until it gained a brief momentary hold over him,
רַק שֶׁהָיָה בַּלְּבוּשׁ שֶׁלּוֹ,
— save that it grabbed only his outer garment,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַתִּתְפְּשֵׂהוּ בְּבִגְדוֹ" (שָׁם לט, יב),
— as stated: “And she caught him by his garment”,
עַד שֶׁהֶרְאָה לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אוֹת אֱמֶת – דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו,
— until Hashem revealed to him the sign of Truth—his father's visage,
וְזֶהוּ "כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי".
— and this is “for You are with me”.

p: וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר עוֹד בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: "בָּאתָה דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו וְכוּלֵי",
— And one can further explain the appearance of his father's visage
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁסִּפְּרוּ מֵרַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ מִלּוּבְּלִין זְכוּתוֹ יָגֵן עָלֵינוּ,
— based on what was related of our holy master the Chozeh of Lublin, may his merit protect us,
שֶׁנִּיצּוֹל מִנִּסָּיוֹן,
— who was saved from a trial
אַף שֶׁנִּדְמָה לוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר עַל פִּי פִּיתּוּי הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
— even though the inclination had framed the act as permissible,
רַק שֶׁנִּזְכַּר שֶׁגָּדַר בַּעֲדוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶׂה דְּבַר רְשׁוּת
— because he remembered the rule he had set never to perform an optional act
שֶׁלֹּא יִצְמַח כְּבוֹד שָׁמַיִם מִמַּעֲשֶׂה זוֹ,
— from which no overt honor of Heaven would flourish,
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵּן פֵּירַשׁ.
— and through that fence he withdrew.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁבָּאתָה דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו,
— And this is why they said his father's visage appeared,
דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, קמב עַמּוּד א):
— for it is stated in the holy Zohar (Part I, 142a):
תָּא חֲזֵי, יַעֲקֹב כָּל עוֹבָדוֹי הֲוָה לִשְׁמָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
— come and see: all deeds of Jacob were exclusively for the Name of the Holy One,
וּבְגִין כָּךְ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא הֲוָה עִמֵּיהּ תָּדִיר דְּלָא אַעְדֵּי מִנֵּיהּ שְׁכִינְתָּא וְכוּלֵי.
— and therefore the Holy One was constantly with him so that the Shechinah never departed from him, etc.
וְכֵן כָּאן בְּיוֹסֵף, שֶׁבָּאתָה דְּיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו
— And so here with Joseph, his father's image reminded him
שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲשׂוֹת דְּבַר רְשׁוּת גַּם כֵּן,
— never to engage even in an optional deed,
וּלְפִי דִּבְרֵי הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע גַּם כֵּן לֹא הָיָה בּוֹ מִצְוָה,
— and even according to the yetzer’s rationalization there was no holy mitzvah here,
וְעַל יְדֵי כֵּן נִיצּוֹל,
— and through this standard he was saved,
וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁעֶנֶת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
— which operates likewise via the staff of Torah words.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Mesillat Yesharim, ch. 20: “This is a most fundamental matter. Know that weighing piety is its difficult task, for its distinctions are subtle and the inclination has great scope to enter here. Its danger is therefore immense: the inclination can distance a person from many good things as though they were evil, and bring many sins near as though they were great mitzvot. In truth, a person can succeed in this weighing only through three things: first, that his heart be utterly upright, with no intention except to give pleasure before the Blessed One, and nothing else; second, that he examine his deeds with great care and strive to correct them according to this purpose; third, that after all this he cast his burden upon God. Then it will be said of him, “Happy is the person whose strength is in You,” and “He does not withhold good from those who walk in integrity.” If he lacks one of these conditions, he will not attain completeness and is close to stumbling and falling. If his intention is not choice and pure, if he neglects the examination he is able to undertake, or if after all this he does not place his trust in his Creator, it is difficult for him not to fall. But if he properly maintains all three—integrity of intention, examination, and trust—he will indeed walk securely and no evil will befall him. This is what Hannah said in her prophecy, “He guards the feet of His faithful ones”; David likewise said, “He will not forsake His faithful ones; they are preserved forever.””

p: וְלִפְעָמִים "רַגְלֵי חֲסִידָיו יִשְׁמֹר" עַל יְדֵי "שִׁבְטְךָ",
— And sometimes Hashem guards the feet of His pious through “Your rod” (affliction),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קעט סוֹף עַמּוּד ב):
— as we find in the holy Zohar at the opening of this parashah (179b):
"רַבּוֹת רָעוֹת צַדִּיק" (תְּהִלִּים לד, כ) – "לַצַּדִּיק" לֹא כְּתִיב אֶלָּא "צַדִּיק" וְכוּלֵי,
— “Many are the ills of the righteous”—it is not written ‘unto the righteous’ but ‘of the righteous’,
תָּא חֲזֵי כַּמָּה בִּישִׁין עָבְרוּ עֲלֵיהּ דְּיַעֲקֹב
— come and see how many tribulations passed over Jacob
בְּגִין דְּלָא יִתְדַּבַּק בְּהַהוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע וְכוּלֵי.
— in order that he not become attached to that evil inclination, etc.
וְכָל עֵסֶק יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה רַק שֶׁתְּהֵא מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵימָה,
— And all the toil of Jacob was solely that his bed be spiritually whole,
שֶׁמִּצִּדּוֹ הָיָה כְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל,
— for personally he was like Adam before the sin,
וְלֹא הָיָה לִמְמוּנָּא דְּעֵשָׂו שׁוּם שְׁלִיטָה בּוֹ רַק בְּיוֹצְאֵי יְרֵכוֹ,
— and the guardian angel of Esau held no power over him except through his descendants,
וְסָבַל כָּל הַסַּבְלָנוּת רַק בִּשְׁבִיל יוֹסֵף.
— so he endured all trials for the sake of Joseph.
וְזֶהוּ "רַבּוֹת רָעוֹת צַדִּיק" –
— And this is “Many are the afflictions of the Tzaddik”—
שֶׁסָּבַל כַּמָּה רָעוֹת בְּמִדַּת צַדִּיק לִכְבּוֹשׁ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע וּלְכוֹבְשׁוֹ,
— enduring numerous afflictions in the attribute of Tzaddik to conquer the yetzer,
"וּמִכֻּלָּם יַצִּילֶנּוּ ה'" (שָׁם),
— “and from them all Hashem delivers him”,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הָרָעוֹת וְהַסַּבְלָנוּת עַל יְדֵי כֵּן נִיצּוֹל,
— for through suffering and patient endurance is one delivered,
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי "שִׁבְטְךָ".
— and this operates through “Your rod”.
וְכֵן הוֹעִיל כָּאן לְיוֹסֵף הַסַּבְלָנוּת שֶׁסָּבַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְהַצִּיל אֶת יוֹסֵף,
— And likewise here the tribulations endured by Jacob availed to deliver Joseph,
וְזֶהוּ "שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי".
— and this is “Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me”.

p: וְכֵן הוּא הָעִנְיָן בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— And such is the dynamic with King David, peace be upon him,
שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת הָיְתָה אֲבִיגַיִל זִיוּוּגוֹ,
— for Abigail was in truth his destined soulmate,
שֶׁהֲרֵי נְשָׂאָהּ אַחַר כָּךְ וְיָלְדָה מִמֶּנּוּ,
— since he subsequently married her and she bore children to him,
וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מָצָא מָקוֹם לְפַתּוֹתוֹ שֶׁהִיא מוּתֶּרֶת לוֹ,
— and the evil inclination found grounds to entice him that she was already permitted,
וּכְעֵין שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּדוֹאֵג שֶׁאָמַר לְשָׁאוּל:
— mirroring what we find in Doeg who argued to Saul:
וְכִי יֵשׁ אִישׁוּת לְדָוִד? וַהֲלֹא מוֹרֵד בַּמַּלְכוּת הוּא וְכוּלֵי,
— “Does marriage apply to David? Behold he is a rebel against the king, etc.,
וְעַכְשָׁיו הַתֵּיר קוּנְעָתוֹ וְכוּלֵי
— and now release his wife, etc.”
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לב, א).
— (as written in Bereishit Rabbah 32:1).
וְכֵן כָּאן מָצָא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע הֶיתֵּר:
— So too here the yetzer found a halakhic pretext:
שֶׁהֲרֵי נָבָל מוֹרֵד בַּמַּלְכוּת הוּא וְחָשׁוּב כְּמֵת וְאִשְׁתּוֹ מוּתֶּרֶת.
— for Nabal was a rebel against the monarchy, deemed halakhically dead, leaving his wife permitted.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (מְגִילָּה יד:):
— And this explains the Talmudic statement (Megillah 14b):
"זֹאת" – מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא אַחֲרִיתָא,
— “this” implies that another incident exists,
וּמַאי נִיהוּ? מַעֲשֵׂה דְּבַת שֶׁבַע,
— and what was it? The episode of Bathsheba,
שֶׁאֲבִיגַיִל הָיְתָה כְּמוֹ בַת שֶׁבַע
— for Abigail was just like Bathsheba,
שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין קז.):
— concerning whom they taught (Sanhedrin 107a):
רְאוּיָה הָיְתָה בַּת שֶׁבַע לְדָוִד מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית וְכוּלֵי,
— Bathsheba was destined for David from the six days of Creation, etc.,
וְכֵן אֲבִיגַיִל רְאוּיָה אֵלָיו וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנְּשָׂאָהּ אַחַר כָּךְ.
— and likewise Abigail was destined for him, as he married her thereafter.
וְזֶה שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ בַּגְּמָרָא לְמַעֲלָתוֹ שֶׁל דָּוִד:
— And this is what the Sages expounded in David's high praise:
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "רַגְלֵי חֲסִידָיו יִשְׁמֹר",
— that Hashem “guards the feet of His pious”,
וְ"לֹא יַעֲזֹב אֶת חֲסִידָיו לְעוֹלָם נִשְׁמָרוּ",
— and “He will not forsake His pious; they are preserved forever”,
שֶׁאַף שֶׁמָּצָא הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מָקוֹם לְפַתּוֹתוֹ,
— for though the yetzer found room to seduce him,
וְהוּא הִרְגִּישׁ בֶּאֱמֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ שַׁיָּיכוּת אֵלָיו וְהִיא זִיוּוּגוֹ,
— and he genuinely sensed that she held a soul-connection to him as his mate,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִצִּילוֹ.
— nevertheless Hashem miraculously delivered him from sin.
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע" –
— And concerning this he declared: “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil”—
שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל פְּגָם זֶה,
— “evil” denoting covenantal blemish,
"כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי" –
— “for You are with me”—
דִּשְׁכִינְתָּא אָתְיָא עִמֵּיהּ וְלֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְּיָדוֹ.
— for the Shechinah accompanies him and will not abandon him to the yetzer's hand.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 14b: “The Gemara asks: The plural term damim, literally, bloods, indicates two. Why did David not use the singular term dam? Rather, this teaches that Abigail revealed her thigh, and he lusted after her, and he went three parasangs by the fire of his desire for her, and said to her: Listen to me, i.e., listen to me and allow me to be intimate with you. Abigail then said to him: ‘Let this not be a stumbling block for you’ (I Samuel 25:31). By inference, from the word ‘this,’ it can be understood that there is someone else who will in fact be a stumbling block for him, and what is this referring to? The incident involving Bathsheba. And in the end this is what was, as indeed he stumbled with Bathsheba. This demonstrates that Abigail was a prophetess, as she knew that this would occur. This also explains why David blessed Abigail for keeping him from being responsible for two incidents involving blood that day: Abigail’s menstrual blood and the shedding of Nabal’s blood.”

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 107a: “Rava taught: What is the meaning of that which is written: ‘For I am ready to stumble (letzela) and my pain is always before me’ (Psalms 38:18)? Bathsheba, daughter of Eliam, was designated as fit for David from the six days of Creation. Rava interprets that the term letzela is referring to Eve, who was taken from the side (tzela) of Adam, the first man, and explains that she was destined for him, just as Eve was destined for Adam. But she came to him through pain. And likewise, the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: Bathsheba, daughter of Eliam, was designated as fit for David, but he partook of her unripe, before the appointed time. David would have ultimately married her in a permitted manner after the death of Uriah.”

p: וְשַׁבָּת הוּא זְמַן תּוֹרָה,
— And Shabbat is the designated time of Torah,
וּדְכוּלֵי עָלְמָא בְּשַׁבַּת נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה (שַׁבָּת פו:),
— and all agree that on Shabbat the Torah was given (Shabbat 86b),
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, מז עַמּוּד ב):
— and in the holy Zohar (Part I, 47b):
"בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי" – דָּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְכוּלֵי.
— “On the seventh day”—this is the Oral Torah, etc.
וּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "ה' לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְיָדוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים לז, לג),
— And that which Scripture states: “Hashem will not leave him in his hand” (Psalms 37:33),
שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ עַל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁצוֹפֶה לַצַּדִּיק וַה' לֹא יַעַזְבֶנּוּ בְּיָדוֹ,
— which was expounded on the yetzer watching the righteous while Hashem rescues him,
הוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
— is achieved specifically through the power of Torah words,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, רב עַמּוּד א):
— and as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 202a):
דְּהָא לֵית לָךְ מִלָּה לְתַבְרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא,
— for you have no weapon to shatter the evil inclination except Torah,
וְשַׁבָּת הַזְּמַן לַתּוֹרָה.
— and Shabbat is the supreme time for Torah.
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קצ עַמּוּד א):
— And in the holy Zohar in this parashah (190a):
דִּכְדַק חָמֵי בַּר נָשׁ הִרְהוּרִין בִּישִׁין אָתְיָן לְגַבֵּיהּ,
— that when a man sees wicked thoughts assailing him,
יִתְעַסֵּק בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וּכְדֵין יִתְעַבְּרוּן מִנֵּיהּ,
— he should immerse in Torah and they will immediately pass away from him,
וְיוּכַל לְתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
— and he can rectify through words of Torah
לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁמָר מִקִּטְרוּג הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לְהַבָּא.
— to remain guarded from the incitement of the yetzer henceforth.

p: וְאָמַר בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ:
— And the holy Zohar states:
יוֹסֵף אֲזַל לְגֵיא צַלְמָוֶת, וְנַחֲתוּ לֵיהּ לְמִצְרַיִם, שְׁכִינְתָּא הֲוַת עִמֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵי.
— Joseph walked into the valley of the shadow of death, they brought him down to Egypt, yet the Shechinah was with him, etc.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיוֹסֵף, שֶׁיָּרַד לְמִצְרַיִם שֶׁהִיא תַּכְלִית הַקְּלִיפָּה – עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ,
— Meaning that Joseph, who descended into Egypt which was the ultimate dark husk—the licentious nakedness of the earth,
וְהָיָה אִישׁ אֶחָד בֵּין כַּמָּה טְמֵאִים וְהָיוּ לוֹ כַּמָּה נִסְיוֹנוֹת,
— and was a single isolated man among myriad impure pagans facing repeated trials,
וְעִם כָּל זֶה לֹא תְאֻנֶּה לוֹ רָעָה, "כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי".
— yet despite all this no evil befell him, “for You are with me”.
שֶׁבְּכָל הַיְּרִידוֹת הָיְתָה הַשְּׁכִינָה בְּיִחוּד עִמּוֹ,
— For throughout all descents the Shechinah was uniquely bonded with him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה פו, ד):
— as written in Bereishit Rabbah (86:4):
"וַיְהִי ה' אֶת יוֹסֵף" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לט, ב) –
— “And Hashem was with Joseph” (Genesis 39:2) –
הָא עִם שְׁאָר שְׁבָטִים לָאו? וְכוּלֵי,
— was He then not with the other tribes? etc.,
מָשָׁל לְרוֹעֶה שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה בְּהֵמוֹת טְעוּנוֹת יַיִן,
— parable to a shepherd who had twelve animals laden with wine,
נִכְנְסָה אַחַת מֵהֶן לַחֲנוּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
— one of them entered into the shop of an idolater,
הִנִּיחַ אַחַד עָשָׂר וְהָלַךְ לוֹ אַחֲרֶיהָ וְכוּלֵי,
— he left the eleven and ran after that solitary one, etc.,
כִּי הַשְּׁאָר בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וְכוּלֵי;
— because the others were safe in the public domain, etc.;
וְכֵן הַשְּׁבָטִים בִּרְשׁוּת אֲבִיהֶם,
— and so the brothers were protected under their father’s authority,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יוֹסֵף בִּרְשׁוּת עַצְמוֹ וּבְאֶרֶץ רְחוֹקָה,
— whereas Joseph was on his own in a remote, corrupt land,
לְפִיכָךְ נִתְיַיחֵד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עִמּוֹ לְשָׁמְרוֹ.
— therefore the Holy One uniquely attached His presence with him to safeguard him.

Rabbi Yudan said: (This is analogous) to an animal driver, who had twelve animals laden with wine before him. One of them entered the shop of an idolater; he forsook the eleven and followed after it. They said to him: ‘Why do you forsake eleven (animals) and follow the one?’ He said to them: ‘These are in the public domain, and I am not concerned lest (the wine) become libation wine.’ So, these (Joseph’s brothers) were adults, and in their father’s domain, but this one was young and on his own. They said: ‘Anyone who jumps on it can take everything that is on it.’ There was a certain clever man there. He said to them: ‘You are looking at what is on it. I am looking at its teeth.’ Rabbi Berekhya said: All the power of that she-bear is in that it is able to jump, and you are greater that it. Astonishing!”

p: וּבָזֶה יוּכְלוּ לִבְטֹוחַ פְּרָטֵי נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁגּוֹלִים לְאֶרֶץ רְחוֹקָה בֵּין הָעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת,
— And through this can individual souls exiled to distant lands among the nations find absolute trust,
כִּי בְּאִם שֶׁיִּתְּנוּ דַּעְתָּם לְהַחֲזִיק בִּמְעוּזָּם,
— for if they resolve to hold fast to their spiritual fortress,
בְּוַדַּאי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִהְיֶה בְכִסְלָם וְיִהְיוּ נִשְׁמָרִים מִכָּל רָע,
— Hashem will surely be their confidence and they will be guarded from all evil,
כְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי".
— as stated: “for You are with me”.
"שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי" –
— “Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me”—
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁבֶט מוּסָר יִהְיֶה לוֹ עִילּוּי וּמִשְׁעֶנֶת בּוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.
— that through the chastising rod of discipline comes spiritual elevation and true reliance upon Him, blessed be His Name.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מד, כא)
— And as they taught in Bereishit Rabbah (44:21)
שֶׁאַבְרָהָם לֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ בַּמֶּה לִבְרוֹר: בְּגֵיהִנָּם אוֹ בְּגָלִיּוֹת,
— that Abraham did not know which to choose: Gehenna or exiles,
עַד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבְרוֹר גָּלִיּוֹת.
— until the Holy One instructed him to choose exiles.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה הָיָה יוֹתֵר טוֹב גֵּיהִנָּם
— Seemingly Gehenna would have been preferable,
שֶׁאֵין פַּחַד לְהִתְקַלְקֵל שָׁם יוֹתֵר כְּמוֹ בְּגָלוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ חֲשָׁשׁ נִסְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁיִּתְקַלְקְלוּ;
— for there is no fear of further moral deterioration there, unlike exile where trials threaten moral ruin;
אוּלָם מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבְּגֵיהִנָּם אֵין תִּקְוָה שֶׁיֵּיטִיב מַעֲשָׂיו מֵעַתָּה,
— however in Gehenna there is no prospect of actively improving one's deeds henceforth,
כִּי "אֵין מַעֲשֶׂה וְגוֹמֵר בִּשְׁאוֹל וְגוֹמֵר" (קֹהֶלֶת ט, י),
— for “there is no work... in the grave (Sheol), etc.” (Ecclesiastes 9:10),
וְהֲגַם שֶׁלֹּא יִתְקַלְקֵל יוֹתֵר, אֲבָל אֵין תִּקְוָה שֶׁיְּתַקֵּן;
— and though he will not deteriorate further, there is no opportunity to rectify;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּגָלוּת שֶׁיֵּשׁ תִּקְוָה שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְעַלּוֹת בִּקְדוּשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁבֶט מוּסָר כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
— whereas in exile there is vibrant hope that one can ascend in holiness via the disciplining rod as mentioned above.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Divrei Soferim §16: “A Jew must not despair of anything, whether in bodily matters—as they said, even when a sharp sword rests upon a person’s neck he should not withhold himself from seeking mercy—or in matters of the soul. Even if he has sunk wherever he has sunk, and sinned in a matter of which the Sages said that repentance is of no avail, God forbid, or his repentance is difficult, or he sees himself sinking further into worldly affairs, he must not despair and say that he can no longer withdraw. There is no despair at all for a Jew, and the blessed God can help in every circumstance. The entire building of the nation of Israel came after complete loss of hope, for Abraham and Sarah were old. … In truth this came from God: the nation was to be built specifically after hope was completely lost, when no person, even Sarah, believed that she would still be remembered with a child. For this is the whole character of the Israelite: to believe that one must never despair, that God can always help, and that nothing is beyond God.”

God brought the nation into being after the apparent end of all natural possibility; Rav Tzadok applies that pattern to spiritual deterioration as well. p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (פד, ב):
— And this is what they taught in Midrash Rabbah at the opening of this parashah (84:2):
"נָסוּ וְאֵין רֹדֵף וְגוֹמֵר" (מִשְׁלֵי כח, א),
— “The wicked flee when no man pursues, etc.” (Proverbs 28:1),
דִּכְתִיב: "וַיֵּלֶךְ אֶל אֶרֶץ מִפְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב אָחִיו" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לו, ו) – מִפְּנֵי שְׁטַר חוֹב,
— for it is written: “and went into a country from the face of his brother Jacob”—fleeing the promissory note of exile;
וְאָמַר עַל זֶה: עָרַק רַשִּׁיעָא וְלָא רָדִיפִין לֵיהּ,
— and the Midrash remarks: the wicked one fled while none pursued him,
כִּי לֹא הָיָה הַמְכֻוָּון עָלָיו
— because the divine objective did not apply to him,
שֶׁאֵין תִּקְוָה וְתוֹעֶלֶת בּוֹ שֶׁיֵּיטִיב מַעֲשָׂיו עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁבֶט מוּסָר.
— as there was neither hope nor utility that he would improve his ways through the chastising rod.
"וְצַדִּיקִים כִּכְפִיר יִבְטָח" (מִשְׁלֵי שָׁם) –
— “but the righteous are bold as a lion” (Proverbs ibid.) –
"וַיֵּשֶׁב יַעֲקֹב" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, א),
— “And Jacob dwelt” (Genesis 37:1),
שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב קִבֵּל עַל עַצְמוֹ בִּרְצוֹן נַפְשׁוֹ עוֹל הַשְּׁטַר חוֹב,
— for Jacob willingly embraced upon himself the burden of the promissory note of servitude,
שֶׁיָּדַע וְהָיָה בּוֹטֵחַ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
— knowing and trusting in Hashem, blessed be He,
שֶׁבָּנָיו לֹא יִתְקַלְקְלוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם,
— that his children would not perish spiritually in Egypt,
אֶלָּא אַדְּרַבָּה, יִתְעַלּוּ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת וּכִדְבָרֵינוּ.
— but on the contrary, would ascend through this into holiness with heightened vigor, according to our words.
וְזֶהוּ "שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי".
— And this is “Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me”.
